# Motion & Interaction Craft

You are a motion engineer. Unacknowledged interactions are a failure state; a static interface can be the right choice when motion adds no information. Make actions responsive, state changes understandable, and waits legible. Aim for smooth rendering and honor reduced-motion preferences.

This skill is craft-first: concrete starting values, curves, and adaptable code examples. When the brief is vague ("add some animations", "make it feel premium"), choose a proportionate motion budget and justify it using the doctrine below. Some §13 recipes are sketches, not complete drop-in implementations; confirm dependencies and event lifecycle before use.

## 适用场景

- **范围判断**：这是为真实界面中的交互或状态变化决定“是否动、如何动、如何验证”的技能；若用户只要静态视觉、视频作品或完整 UI 重设计，不应仅因出现“高级感”“有节奏”之类措辞就调用动效流程。
- 从零给页面/组件加动效：hover、按压、转场、弹出、共享元素
- 修复"感觉不对"的动效：太慢、太快、生硬、抖动、闪烁、廉价
- 设计等待与反馈动效：loading 骨架屏、spinner、toast、错误抖动、成功勾选
- 滚动编排：入场 reveal、pin、卡片堆叠、scrub 文字、视差、跑马灯
- 微交互规格交付：trigger → rules → feedback → loops，直接给工程实现
- 动效 code review / lint：对已有动效代码跑 §14 清单
- 整页设计时辅助判断节奏与层级（§1b，可选；不用于单一组件动效任务）
- 判断某个页面/项目**适合哪些动效、动效预算给多少**（选择，而非堆砌）
- 为页面提炼有依据的动效概念，避免通用淡入上移套遍所有场景；允许结论是无需签名动效
- 为特定受众推导动效语言（如家长端亲子 App：温柔有陪伴感而非幼稚）
- 设计签名角色/生命化动效（吉祥物呼吸眨眼、数据生长、融色切换）
- 交付前**按风险自查验证**：小改动验证相关交互；复杂状态/滚动动效增加浏览器与边界 case 检查

**不适用**：视频/节目时间线制作与导出（用 video-hyperframes / remotion）；3D/WebGL 场景动画（threejs / shader-dev）；纯静态视觉稿（canvas-design）；整页 UI/品牌的从零设计或整体改版（用相应设计流程，本 Skill 只负责其中的动效）；状态体系“该有哪些状态”的枚举与审计（用 web-interaction-states）；只修改文案、颜色、间距等不涉及运动或交互反馈的任务。界面需要静态、即时反馈时不必为使用本 Skill 强加动画。

## 来源/改编

**本轮动效概念补充的参考**（以下「概念句式/筛选门」是本 skill 基于资料整理的方法，不是原文中的专有术语）：
- [Nielsen Norman Group — Animation for Attention and Comprehension](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/animation-usability/)：选动效前判断注意力位置、目标、出现频率与触发方式；动效可解释状态和因果，但反复观看会妨碍任务。
- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines — Motion](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/motion.md)：有目的、简短精准、不遮盖体验；频繁交互避免强动效，重要信息不能只靠动画表达，尽可能允许打断。
- [IBM Carbon — Motion](https://carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/foundations/motion/)：区分日常任务的 productive motion 与少数关键时刻的 expressive motion；从产品目标、信息层级、旅程和关键时刻选择动效并测试。

- **interaction-design 插件**（designer-skills，Gemini 格式）：取其 `animation-principles`（easing/duration/stagger）、`micro-interaction-spec`（trigger-rules-feedback-loops 框架）、`feedback-patterns`、`loading-states`、`interfaces-that-feel`（动效即情感信号）、`gesture-patterns`（阈值与反馈）的 craft 规则，去掉插件间的互相引用，整合进本文件对应章节。
- **motion-system**（designer-skills / design-systems）：duration 与 easing token 体系、choreography 规则、系统级 reduced-motion 处理，落为 §3 可粘贴的 CSS 变量。
- **taste-skill**（`gpt-tasteskill` + `soft-skill`）：借鉴 ScrollTrigger、磁性按钮与性能检查；其中绝对化的属性/缓动/库禁令改为有条件的建议（§1、§8、§11）。
- **figma-use-motion / figma-implement-motion**（agent-skills）：仅取可移植部分——easing 词汇表与"默认保持动效克制（0.25–0.7s、stagger 代替齐动）"的默认值；Figma 插件 API 专属内容（manualKeyframeTracks 等）已剔除。
- **格式改编**：由 Gemini 插件格式（`.gemini/extensions` + commands 目录）转为标准 Agent Skill 单文件；原交叉引用改为章节索引；§13 提供可改造的 Web 配方（token、IO reveal、FLIP、count-up、WAAPI 降级），其中部分为示意片段，使用前需补齐上下文。
- **整页构图提示（§1b）**：借鉴 taste-skill 与 anti-ui-slop 的层级和节奏思路；现为可选设计提示，仅在整页创作且无现有视觉系统时参考，不作为组件动效的验收条件。
- **语境化动效语言与签名角色（§1c Step 2b / §1d / §15，第三轮补充）**：来自家长端「我的」会员卡方案的实战迭代——用户反馈"通用动效不适用 + 有 bug + 没有为这个产品设计"后补充：(1) 从受众情感状态推导动效语言（家长端 = 温柔有陪伴感、可爱但不幼稚，受众≠受益者）；(2) 签名伙伴「芽芽」模式（idle 呼吸/眨眼 + reactive 跳动，装饰内层裁切、角色不被裁剪）；(3) 数据生命化（数字滚动 + 小芽生长）与"融而不切"（颜料滴 + 交叉融色）；(4) §15 自查验证门（静态 + headless/CDP 运行时 + 边界 case，bug 由交付方自己找），以及 carousel 状态卫生三坑（指针倾斜残留、snap 对齐混用、单项不隐藏页码）。

---

## 1. Doctrine — Rules by strength

**Must:** provide timely feedback for user actions; preserve keyboard access and essential status information; honor reduced motion; clean up listeners and temporary nodes; verify that the interaction works. These are delivery requirements, not an invitation to animate every element.

**Default:** use named properties instead of `transition: all`; prefer transform/opacity for movement; keep feedback short and exits faster than entrances; choose a motion budget before coding. Override a default when the component or content calls for it, and state why.

**Optional:** scroll theatre, magnetic controls, mascots, melt transitions, and the page-composition ideas in §1b. Use only where the audience, brand, task, and device justify them. Never add an effect merely to satisfy a checklist.

Avoid these common failure modes:

- ❌ `transition: all` — may animate unrelated properties. Name the properties you intend to transition.
- ❌ `linear` or default `ease-in-out` for every interaction — choose a curve based on the transition; linear is useful for continuous progress and loops.
- ❌ Unexplained state changes — simple, immediate changes can be appropriate; a user action still needs timely acknowledgment.
- ❌ Animating layout on every frame when a transform can express the same movement. Layout/paint animation is acceptable when necessary and measured (§11).
- ❌ Raw scroll listeners doing unthrottled layout reads/writes for reveals. Use IntersectionObserver for entry detection (§8).
- ❌ Missing press or equivalent immediate feedback on actionable controls — acknowledge within ~100ms.
- ❌ Instant spinner flash on a short action; delay the wait indicator when the result may arrive quickly (§7).
- ❌ Animating without a `prefers-reduced-motion` path (§10).
- ❌ Animation for decoration with no communicative purpose. Every motion says something.
- ❌ Long durations because they look "smooth" in devtools. UI motion is fast: 100–500ms is the working range.

## 1b. Page-composition notes (only when designing a whole page)

Skip this section when changing only an existing component or its motion. Motion should follow the page's design system, not override it. When building a whole page and no visual direction exists, avoid mechanical repetition; consider the following prompts as options, not pass/fail rules:

1. **Vary structure where content calls for it.** Consider full-bleed features, asymmetric splits, editorial columns, timelines, definition rows, or a restrained grid. Repeated structures can be useful when comparison or scanning is the goal.
2. **Create hierarchy appropriate to the content.** Give key moments enough scale and whitespace without imposing a fixed headline length or ratio.
3. **Use rhythm intentionally.** Vary density or section treatment when chapters differ; preserve continuity when content belongs together.
4. **Use a meaningful visual layer when available.** Imagery, diagrams, data visuals, or pull-quotes can carry information; do not invent decoration to meet a quota.
5. **Let grids serve the task.** Mixed spans can work for storytelling; equal cells can be better for comparable items. Do not force `grid-auto-flow: dense` if it disrupts logical or keyboard reading order.
6. **Make labels informative.** Avoid ornamental numbering without meaning; keep real section and process labels.
7. **Add detail only where it clarifies affordance.** Nested surfaces, icon treatments, and eyebrow tags are optional, subject to the existing visual system.
8. **Choose alignment deliberately.** An asymmetric emphasis can add character; a centered or equal-column layout may be right for a compact task or comparable data.
9. **Whole-page pre-flight:** note the hierarchy and section rhythm; change repetition only when it obscures meaning or makes navigation monotonous.

## 1c. Motion Selection — think before you animate

The rules above tell you HOW to animate well. This tells you WHETHER to animate at all, and how much. Applying the full arsenal to every page is its own failure mode: a dashboard with pinned scroll sections is worse than one with none.

### Step 1 — Classify the brief

Use the table as a starting range, not a quota. Existing product conventions and the user's stated requirements take precedence.

| Deliverable | Motion budget |
|---|---|
| Marketing / landing page | Flexible: state feedback plus a purposeful signature moment if the content supports one. Scroll effects are optional. |
| Product tool / dashboard / admin | Restraint: state feedback, meaningful data transitions. Avoid entrances or pinning that delay work. |
| Talk / presentation page | Choreograph only moments that support the spoken narrative; account for talk length and manual pacing. |
| Form / checkout / flow | Functional: validation, step transitions, submit and recovery feedback. |
| Editorial / article / docs | Subtle: preserve reading flow; consider image reveals where they add orientation. |
| Portfolio / showcase | Expressive when the work calls for it; prioritize clear browsing and one coherent motion idea. |
| Kids / playful consumer | Clear, playful feedback can fit; test comprehension and sensory load with the actual audience. |
| Enterprise / finance / medical / govt | Predictable, restrained feedback; avoid effects that obscure serious information or slow tasks. |

### Step 2 — Ask before choosing

1. **Is the user here to read or to use?** Reading → motion can support content orientation. Using → motion primarily supports feedback and state. Mixed tasks may need both.
2. **Does motion interfere with the core task?** Dense data, long forms, frequent actions → cut motion, not add it.
3. **Device and performance context?** Mobile-first, low-end, projector, kiosk → shorter durations, fewer simultaneous movers, cheaper properties.
4. **Brand tone?** Playful may suit restrained springs; serious contexts usually favor predictable curves and little or no overshoot.
5. **WHO is the user, emotionally?** Derive the motion language from the audience's felt state, not from the app category alone (Step 2b).

### Step 2b — Derive the motion language from the audience

Pick ONE adjective the motion should feel like, then let it drive curves, durations, and behavior:

| Audience / context | Motion language | Concrete rules |
|---|---|---|
| 家长端 / 亲子产品（用户是父母） | 温柔、有陪伴感 | 柔和减速、可选低幅弹性（200–350ms）；已有角色且确有陪伴需求时才考虑轻微氛围循环；可爱但**不幼稚** |
| 儿童直接使用 | 活泼、直白 | 明确反馈、稍大位移、庆祝动效 OK；仍遵守 100ms 反馈底线 |
| 效率工具 / 开发者 | 快、准、安静 | 状态反馈为主，禁氛围循环动画 |
| 金融 / 医疗 / 政企 | 稳、可预期 | 无 overshoot、无循环、无 scrub |
| 内容 / 阅读 | 安静、不抢戏 | 只做显现与过渡，禁弹跳 |
| 品牌 / 活动 | 张扬、有记忆点 | 一个签名时刻，其余克制 |

**Audience ≠ end beneficiary**: a parent app about kids is used by adults — the cute lives in the CONTENT (mascot, illustrations), the motion stays warm and restrained. Getting this backwards (childish motion in a parent app) is the most common context error.

Whether a signature device is warranted is decided in Step 3; §1d contains optional patterns, not a menu to select from before understanding the page.

### Step 3 — Derive a motion concept (when the scope warrants one)

A motion concept is a **small rule for how change behaves in this particular interface**, grounded in its content and interaction, not a theme word, a visual metaphor to apply everywhere, or a request for more animation. For multi-element work, derive it **after** identifying the task/audience and **before** picking effects or curves. For a single button fix, use the existing design language and skip the concept exercise.

1. **Collect evidence from the actual page:** what changes in the user's journey, the content's real relationships (e.g. draft → published, item → collection, source → result), existing shapes/materials/typography, brand tone, and interaction frequency. If the project already has a motion language, extend it instead of inventing a second one. Do not fabricate a story from generic category labels alone.
2. **Describe the job before the metaphor:** *“When [real trigger/state], [specific thing] changes in [observable way], so [user understands/feels something relevant].”* Name an observable behavior (origin, direction, pace, continuity, hold), not just “premium”, “flowing”, or “cinematic”. A content metaphor is optional; it must clarify a real relationship.
3. **Generate two genuinely different candidates, then select or reject:** compare how each explains the state change, fits the page, and behaves on the tenth repetition. One can be *“no signature; direct state feedback only.”* Do not mix candidates into a pile of effects. If neither improves comprehension or tone without friction, choose the quiet option.
4. **Choose one home for expression:** one key transition or interaction may carry the concept; routine hover, form inputs, loading, and errors stay consistent and fast. Expressiveness can come from a subtle origin, timing contrast, hold, or continuity—not distance, bounce, or quantity. Repeated and indirectly triggered motion receives a smaller budget than a rare, user-initiated moment.
5. **Run the concept filter:** Where is attention when it starts? What does it explain that a static change would not? How often will it recur? Does it remain useful on a small screen, with keyboard/touch, reduced motion, and rapid repeat? Can the user interrupt it without waiting? If an answer is weak, simplify or remove the effect.

**Examples (hypothetical; adapt to the actual product, not its category):**

| Observed relationship | Possible concept | Quiet implementation |
|---|---|---|
| An editor moves a draft into a published list | “The draft retains its identity as it joins the collection.” | On publish, the source item becomes/points to the list row; no full-page celebration. |
| A user changes the time range of a chart | “The same measure updates in place.” | Preserve axes/labels where valid; data marks change in place briefly, or switch instantly for rapid comparison. |
| A reader opens a note anchored to a paragraph | “The note stays attached to its source.” | Reveal the note from the anchor with a small local transition; no page-wide text reveal. |
| A busy table has no meaningful spatial relationship to preserve | “Keep the work uninterrupted.” | Immediate state feedback, stable rows, no signature entrance. |

**Anti-template check:** If the concept could be pasted unchanged onto three unrelated products, it is probably a generic effect description. Replace it with an actual content/state relationship, or choose no signature. Do not invent physical behavior (“ink”, “liquid”, “magnetism”) when the product's visual language does not support it.

### Step 4 — Write the budget before coding

For anything beyond a small existing-component fix, make this compact decision record before coding:

| Field | Answer |
|---|---|
| Task and audience | What is the person trying to do, and in what emotional/performance context? |
| Motion job | Which state change or relationship needs clarification? |
| Concept, if warranted | One concrete trigger → behavior → meaning sentence; or “none—direct feedback is clearer.” |
| Budget | Essential feedback; optional signature; effects deliberately excluded. |
| Constraints | Existing design language, input devices, reduced motion, content density, performance. |

Example: *"Dashboard for frequent data entry: no signature concept; immediate control feedback + status transitions; no scroll choreography; reduced motion keeps progress readable."* If the brief is silent, start with **state-feedback-only** and add effects only where content justifies them. For a one-control change, answer these fields mentally and keep the output proportionate.

**Signature over quantity, when warranted**: one purposeful interaction beats five generic ones. If you can't name what each animation communicates, remove it; “none” is a valid result.

## 1d. Life-like & Signature Motion (context-appropriate character)

When the product already uses characters or illustration and warmth/delight is the goal, a **living element with idle + reactive behavior** may work better than adding effects to many static boxes. It is not a default for every warm-feeling product.

**Optional signature companion (mascot / character)** — when the product already has one, consider these behaviors:
- **Idle**: if ambience benefits the experience, breathe subtly (scale 1↔1.03, 3–4s) or blink occasionally; pause when offscreen and stop under reduced motion. Perpetual animation is not automatically harmless.
- **Reactive**: responds to state changes — hops when its card becomes active, waves on hover, hides/shrinks when not relevant. The reaction is the "it notices me" moment.
- **Placement**: pokes from a card corner or content edge as a "sticker" — requires the animated container NOT to clip it (wrap decorations in an inner clipped layer, keep the character outside it, §13).

**Data-as-life** — where appropriate, a number can roll once after an update or an illustration can respond to completion. Keep exact values immediately available as text, and avoid motion that makes changing metrics harder to read.

**Optional melt transition** — for an atmospheric mode change, a short ripple/crossfade (~280ms) can express continuity. For rapid filters, data views, and reduced motion, a direct state change is often more legible.

**Restraint rule**: use as few signatures as the experience needs; do not stack all three treatments by default.

## 2. The Decision Order (before writing any code)

0. **Choose a concept and budget (§1c)** — classify the deliverable, answer the context questions, derive the motion language, and, for multi-element work, compare grounded concept candidates including “none”. Only then decide whether a signature is warranted and write the budget. Later steps operate inside it.
1. **What changed?** Identify the state transition (appear / disappear / move / change / progress / respond-to-input).
2. **How long?** Pick from the duration scale (§3) by element size and importance — not by feel.
3. **Which curve?** Enter = decelerate, exit = accelerate, move = in-out, tactile = spring (§4).
4. **What's the feedback?** Every user action gets acknowledgment within 100ms (§6).
5. **Reduced motion?** Define the fallback before shipping (§10).
6. **Perf check?** Prefer compositor-friendly movement; measure justified layout/paint effects, particularly on lower-end devices (§11).

---

## 3. Motion Tokens (paste-ready)

Use existing project tokens when available. If the project lacks motion tokens, these are starting values rather than a mandatory global system; 4–6 durations is usually enough.

```css
:root {
  /* Durations */
  --duration-instant: 50ms;   /* press feedback, checkbox tick — must feel immediate */
  --duration-fast: 150ms;     /* hover, tooltip, chip, small fade */
  --duration-normal: 250ms;   /* default: dropdown, toggle, focus ring, card */
  --duration-moderate: 350ms; /* modal, drawer, panel slide */
  --duration-slow: 500ms;     /* page-level transition, complex choreography */
  --duration-deliberate: 700ms; /* high-emphasis moments only (onboarding reveal) */

  /* Easings — semantic, not generic */
  --ease-standard: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1);      /* most UI state changes */
  --ease-enter: cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1);         /* elements entering (decelerate) */
  --ease-exit: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1);          /* elements leaving (accelerate) */
  --ease-move: cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1);      /* moving between positions */
  --ease-spring: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1); /* tactile overshoot: FAB, toggle, pop */
  --ease-linear: linear;                            /* constant-rate progress and loops */

  /* Choreography */
  --stagger: 40ms; /* per-item offset in a sequence; total sequence ≤ 500ms */
}
```

**Duration selection rules**:
| Element | Duration | Easing |
|---|---|---|
| Button press / checkbox feedback | 50–100ms | standard |
| Toggle knob travel | 150–250ms | standard or restrained spring |
| Hover, tooltip, icon swap | 100–200ms | standard/enter |
| Dropdown, menu, popover | 150–250ms | enter (in) / exit (out) |
| Modal, drawer, sheet | 250–400ms | enter/exit |
| Page transition, shared element | 300–500ms | move |
| Scroll-reveal (per element) | 400–700ms | enter |

Exit animations are faster than entrances (~70%): users don't wait for things to leave.

---

## 4. Easing Selection Guide

Curves are emotional decisions:

- **ease-out / decelerate** (`cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)`) — default for entrances. Elements arrive fast, settle softly. "Something soft landing."
- **ease-in / accelerate** — exits only. Element leaves with momentum.
- **ease-in-out** — position changes (A→B on screen) when symmetric travel makes sense; avoid applying it indiscriminately.
- **spring / overshoot** (`cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)`) — playful, tactile, confident. Use for: toggles, FAB expand, like-button pop, drawer bounce-in. Overshoot must be small (5–10% of travel) or it reads as cartoonish.
- **linear** — constant-rate progress and loops (spinner rotation, shimmer sweep, marquee). Usually avoid it for an element that visibly lands.

**Spring physics parameters** (when using JS springs — Framer Motion, react-spring, WAAPI with spring()):
- Stiff spring: high stiffness, moderate damping → snappy, confident (buttons, toggles). Settle ≤ 400ms.
- Loose spring: low stiffness, low damping → playful, forgiving (like bursts, drag release). Settle ≤ 700ms.
- Always critically-dampable: no infinite oscillation on UI chrome.

## 5. Interaction Motion by Element

### Button (the most-audited element)
```css
.btn {
  transition: transform var(--duration-instant) var(--ease-standard),
              background-color var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-standard),
              box-shadow var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-standard);
}
.btn:hover { background-color: var(--btn-hover); }
.btn:active { transform: scale(0.97); }        /* prompt press acknowledgment */
.btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }
.btn:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }
.btn.is-loading { pointer-events: none; }        /* lock + spinner in label */
```
- Hover = a subtle color or shadow change by default; use other cues when the existing component language calls for them.
- Never remove `:focus-visible`. Style it deliberately.
- Disabled: explain why when it is not obvious; ensure the explanation is available without relying on a tooltip attached only to a disabled control.

### Magnetic / kinetic button (premium feel, desktop)
On pointermove within a radius, translate the button toward the cursor by 10–20% of the distance; inner icon translates an extra 2–4px diagonally. Use `transform: translate3d()`, spring back on leave. Pointer-fine only (`@media (pointer: fine)`), skip on touch and reduced-motion.

### Toggle / switch
Knob travels with `--ease-spring`, 150–250ms. Track color crossfades. Add a subtle scale punch on the knob at midpoint (scale 1.05 → 1).

### Card (hover response)
When imagery exists, clip an inner image layer and scale it subtly over 400–600ms; optionally lift the container by `translateY(-2px)` if elevation is part of the design system. If a character or badge extends beyond the card, clip only the inner decoration, not the outer card (§13).

### Modal / drawer / sheet
- Backdrop: opacity 0→1, 150–250ms.
- Panel: enter with `--ease-enter`, from `translateY(16px) scale(0.98)` (dialog) or `translateX(100%)` (drawer); exit mirrors at ~70% duration with `--ease-exit`.
- Focus: trap inside, restore to trigger on close. Escape closes.
- Exit animation must complete before DOM removal; when using discrete CSS transitions, test support and provide a fallback. `@starting-style` handles entry, while `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` plus the appropriate `display` transition can support exit in compatible browsers.

### Dropdown / popover / tooltip
Tooltip: fade + `translateY(4px)`, 100–150ms, `--ease-enter`. Never animate tooltip on scroll (reposition instantly).

### Tabs / segmented control
Active indicator slides between positions (`--ease-move`, 200–300ms) — one shared indicator element, not per-tab fades. Content crossfades 150ms.

### Nav active state
Indicator bar slides/expands to the active item; active label weight change. Distinguishable by more than color.

### Accordion
If the content must expand, `grid-template-rows: 0fr → 1fr` or a measured-height transition can be appropriate; they incur layout work, so keep the region small and test with dynamic content. Use 250–350ms `--ease-standard`; rotate the chevron with the same duration. For dense or frequently toggled lists, an immediate disclosure may be clearer.

## 6. Feedback Motion (acknowledge every action)

**Timing rule**: every user action gets perceptible acknowledgment within ~100ms. The cue can be a pressed appearance, changed label, progress state, or motion; success confirmation may come later.

| Event | Motion | Spec |
|---|---|---|
| Press | scale 0.97 / darken | 50–100ms |
| Toggle | knob slide + track fill | 150–250ms spring |
| Success | checkmark draw (SVG stroke-dashoffset) + subtle scale pop | 300–500ms |
| Error | horizontal shake, 3 decays, amplitude 4→1px | 400ms, then inline message |
| Copy / save | icon swap + toast | toast 3–5s auto-dismiss |
| Like | heart scale pop (1→1.2→1) + particle burst (optional, ≤600ms) | spring |
| Upload | progress ring/bar + % count-up | determinate |
| Undo | toast with action button, 5s window | — |

**Toast recipe** (transform/opacity only):
```css
.toast {
  transform: translateY(8px); opacity: 0;
  transition: transform var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-enter), opacity var(--duration-fast);
}
.toast.show { transform: translateY(0); opacity: 1; }
```

**Error shake recipe**:
```css
@keyframes shake {
  0%, 100% { transform: translateX(0); }
  25% { transform: translateX(-4px); }
  50% { transform: translateX(4px); }
  75% { transform: translateX(-2px); }
}
.shake { animation: shake 400ms var(--ease-standard); }
```

**Checkmark draw**:
```css
.check-path { stroke-dasharray: 20; stroke-dashoffset: 20; transition: stroke-dashoffset 400ms var(--ease-enter); }
.check-path.drawn { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
```

Feedback hierarchy (prefer the top): inline at the source → within component → toast/banner → system notification. Errors persist until resolved; toasts 3–5s. Never color-only.

---

## 7. Loading Motion

| Wait | What to show |
|---|---|
| <100ms | nothing |
| 100–400ms | immediate pressed/busy acknowledgment; if still waiting, show a subtle indicator after a short delay rather than flashing a spinner |
| 400ms–3s | skeleton for known content geometry, or one localized spinner/label; button enters loading state |
| >3s | determinate progress + label; cancel option |
| >10s | progress + time estimate + background option |

**Skeleton shimmer** (optional; reduced-motion: static shape, no sweep):
```css
.skeleton {
  background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--sk-1) 25%, var(--sk-2) 50%, var(--sk-1) 75%);
  background-size: 200% 100%;
  animation: shimmer 1.4s var(--ease-linear) infinite;
  border-radius: 4px;
}
@keyframes shimmer { to { background-position: -200% 0; } }
```
- Skeleton shapes should approximate the real content's geometry (prevents layout shift on swap); use them only when the layout is known and the wait is long enough to perceive them.
- Crossfade content in (~150ms) if it avoids a jarring swap; instant replacement can be clearer for dense or frequent updates. Stagger only when it helps scanning.
- Spinner: one per view, small, unobtrusive. Progress: determinate when measurable.
- Optimistic UI: apply expected result instantly, reconcile on response, roll back with a visible reversal (not a silent snap-back).
- Pull-to-refresh: rubber-band resistance past threshold, spinner tracks pull distance, snap-back on release below threshold.

---

## 8. Scroll & Page Motion

**Reveal on enter:** Use the progressive-enhancement code in §13. It keeps content visible without JS, in print, and under reduced motion; set a short stagger only when sequential attention helps.
- Stagger 30–50ms per item; total sequence ≤ 500ms; lead with the most important element.
- Reveal distance is small (16–24px). Big slides read as gimmicky.
- Re-triggering: reveal-once for content, re-reveal only for hero-level moments.

**Scroll-linked (GSAP ScrollTrigger patterns):**
- **Pin + scroll**: pin a section title left while a gallery scrolls right — `ScrollTrigger pin: true`; use `scrub: 0.5–1` when catch-up smoothing fits. `scrub: true` maps directly to scroll position and can be preferable when precise tracking matters.
- **Image scale & fade**: images start `scale: 0.8`, grow to 1 in view, darken to `opacity: 0.2` scrolling out.
- **Text scrub reveal**: if justified in short display copy, reveal words sequentially with scroll; avoid making article or essential text unreadable while scrolling.
- **Card stacking**: cards overlap and stack upward as you scroll — each card pins while the next slides over.
- **Marquee**: continuous row, `--ease-linear`, pause on hover, duplicated content for seamless loop.
- **Horizontal guard**: prevent accidental horizontal overflow at its source or clip only the animated section; avoid page-wide clipping that hides focus rings, sticky elements, or intentional overflow.

**View Transitions API** (same-document navigations, where supported):
```js
document.startViewTransition(() => updateDOM());
```
```css
::view-transition-old(root), ::view-transition-new(root) { animation-duration: 300ms; }
```
Shared-element transitions for card→detail via `view-transition-name`. Where unsupported, preserve a functional instant navigation; a CSS crossfade is optional.

**Page enter**: hero elements stagger in 40ms apart, total ≤ 500ms, `--ease-enter`.

---

## 9. Gesture Feedback

- **Immediate response on gesture start** — the element tracks the finger from frame one.
- **Thresholds**: 10–15px travel before activation; velocity threshold for flicks; direction lock after initial movement (scroll vs swipe).
- **Rubber-banding**: past the boundary, resistance increases (movement = distance × 0.4 and shrinking).
- **Snap points**: visible indicator when crossing a commit threshold.
- **Cancel zone**: return to origin to abort; completion confirmation on commit.
- **Swipe actions**: reveal action buttons progressively with the drag; full-swipe commits with a distinct snap.
- Long-press: radial progress ring fills over 500ms, then context menu.
- Every gesture has a visible button/menu alternative. Undo for destructive gestures.

---

## 10. Reduced Motion (system preference + component intent)

```css
/* Use tokens so ordinary state transitions become near-instant. */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  :root {
    --duration-instant: 1ms; --duration-fast: 1ms; --duration-normal: 1ms;
    --duration-moderate: 1ms; --duration-slow: 1ms; --duration-deliberate: 1ms;
  }
  html { scroll-behavior: auto; }
  [data-reveal] { opacity: 1; transform: none; transition: none; }
  .skeleton { animation: none; background: var(--sk-1); }
  .mascot, .mascot .eye, .marquee { animation: none; }
  /* Opt out of each decorative/scroll-linked animation in its own selector. */
}
```
Rules: remove nonessential slide/scale/rotation and autoplay loops. Prefer instant changes or short opacity fades. **Preserve the information** in loading/progress states with a stable label or numeric progress; a spinner may remain only if no equivalent status cue exists and it does not create problematic motion. For third-party animations with fixed timings, override those selectors explicitly. Test with the preference enabled before shipping.

---

## 11. Performance Guardrails

- Prefer `transform` and `opacity` for moving elements (often compositor-friendly). Color/background and SVG stroke transitions are reasonable for small UI regions; measured layout animation can be justified for disclosure. Profile large paint areas and repeated layout changes instead of treating any non-transform property as forbidden.
- `will-change: transform` only on elements about to animate, removed after. Never sprinkled globally.
- No layout reads (`offsetHeight`, `getBoundingClientRect`) inside animation frames — batch reads before writes.
- Scroll effects: IntersectionObserver for reveals; ScrollTrigger or CSS scroll timelines where appropriate for scroll-linked motion. If using raw scroll listeners, use passive listeners and rAF scheduling, avoid layout thrash, and measure the result.
- Test on a low-powered device, not just devtools. What's smooth in design tools is janky in production.
- Concurrent animations: keep the number of moving elements proportionate to the device and task; stagger when it improves comprehension rather than as a universal rule.

---

## 12. Motion as Emotional Signal

Easing communicates intent; motion carries mood. Use when the UI is correct but cold.

**Timing principles**:
- Good news is instant; heavy news arrives slowly (600ms+ with weight).
- After an error: 300–600ms of recovery space before the next prompt.
- Never make the user feel responsible for a system failure — the copy owns it.
- Micro-wins get acknowledged; don't absorb them silently.
- The loading state sets expectations — match its mood to what's coming ("Getting your data…" not "Loading…").

**Copy voice by state** (motion and copy are one system):
| State | Voice |
|---|---|
| Loading | Present and calm |
| Empty | Invitational — what belongs here |
| Error (user) | Blame-free, one specific next step |
| Error (system) | Own it, brief apology, path forward |
| Success | Warm and brief |

**Review questions**: What is the person feeling at this state? Does the motion convey intent or fill time? Strip all color — does the signal survive? Would this feel like a person made it?

## 13. Code Recipes (adapt to project lifecycle)

**Press + hover button** — see §5. **Magnetic button** (pointer-fine, spring return):
```js
const canMagnetize = matchMedia('(pointer: fine) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)');
btn.addEventListener('pointermove', (e) => {
  if (!canMagnetize.matches) return;
  const r = btn.getBoundingClientRect();
  const x = (e.clientX - r.left - r.width / 2) * 0.2;
  const y = (e.clientY - r.top - r.height / 2) * 0.2;
  btn.style.transform = `translate3d(${x}px, ${y}px, 0)`;
});
btn.addEventListener('pointerleave', () => { btn.style.transform = ''; }); // CSS transition springs back
canMagnetize.addEventListener('change', () => { if (!canMagnetize.matches) btn.style.transform = ''; });
```
In a mounted component, remove these listeners on unmount; apply magnetism to a wrapper if `:active` also controls the button transform.

**Spring return** (CSS): `transition: transform 400ms cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);`

**Count-up number** (noncritical stats; render the final value directly under reduced motion):
```js
function countUp(el, to, ms = 800) {
  if (matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) {
    el.textContent = String(to);
    return;
  }
  const from = 0, t0 = performance.now();
  const ease = (t) => 1 - Math.pow(1 - t, 3); // ease-out cubic
  function tick(t) {
    const p = Math.min((t - t0) / ms, 1);
    el.textContent = Math.round(from + (to - from) * ease(p));
    if (p < 1) requestAnimationFrame(tick);
  }
  requestAnimationFrame(tick);
}
```
If the value can change during animation, cancel the previous animation before starting another; preserve decimals and units from the actual data.

**Stagger via CSS custom property** — set `--i` per element in a loop, then:
```css
.item { transition-delay: calc(var(--i, 0) * 40ms); }
```

**List reorder (FLIP)** — measure first/last rects, invert with transform, play:
```js
function animateReorder(elements, mutate) {
  const first = new Map(elements.map(el => [el, el.getBoundingClientRect()]));
  mutate(); // Reorder synchronously, then measure new positions.
  if (matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) return;
  for (const [el, r] of first) {
    if (!el.isConnected) continue;
    const now = el.getBoundingClientRect();
    const dx = r.left - now.left, dy = r.top - now.top;
    if (!dx && !dy) continue;
    el.animate([{ transform: `translate(${dx}px, ${dy}px)` }, { transform: 'none' }],
      { duration: 300, easing: 'cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)' });
  }
}
```
If items already have transforms, compose with their existing transform rather than replacing it; frameworks may require measuring after a synchronous commit.

**WAAPI with fallback**: feature-detect `element.animate`; if absent, apply final styles instantly (no animation, not broken UI).

**Robust scroll reveal (progressive enhancement)** — keep content visible by default. Only hide candidates after JS and IO support are confirmed; initialize already-visible items immediately, observe the rest, and expose everything under reduced motion or without JS. Place the CSS below in the page stylesheet before the script runs:
```js
function setupReveals() {
  const revealItems = [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-reveal]')];
  const motionPreference = matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)');
  if (motionPreference.matches || !('IntersectionObserver' in window)) return () => {};
  const io = new IntersectionObserver(entries => {
    for (const entry of entries) {
      if (!entry.isIntersecting) continue;
      entry.target.classList.add('in');
      io.unobserve(entry.target);
    }
  }, { threshold: 0.12, rootMargin: '0px 0px -40px 0px' });
  document.documentElement.classList.add('reveal-ready');
  for (const el of revealItems) {
    const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
    if (r.top < innerHeight * 0.92 && r.bottom > 0) {
      el.classList.add('in');
    } else {
      el.classList.add('reveal-pending');
      io.observe(el);
    }
  }
  const onPreferenceChange = () => {
    if (!motionPreference.matches) return;
    io.disconnect();
    document.documentElement.classList.remove('reveal-ready');
    motionPreference.removeEventListener('change', onPreferenceChange);
  };
  const onPrint = () => document.documentElement.classList.remove('reveal-ready');
  motionPreference.addEventListener('change', onPreferenceChange);
  window.addEventListener('beforeprint', onPrint);
  return () => {
    io.disconnect();
    motionPreference.removeEventListener('change', onPreferenceChange);
    window.removeEventListener('beforeprint', onPrint);
    document.documentElement.classList.remove('reveal-ready');
    revealItems.forEach(el => el.classList.remove('reveal-pending'));
  };
}
const cleanupReveals = setupReveals(); // Call cleanupReveals() before unmount/route teardown.
```
```css
[data-reveal] { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
.reveal-ready [data-reveal].reveal-pending {
  opacity: 0; transform: translateY(20px);
  transition: opacity 600ms var(--ease-enter), transform 600ms var(--ease-enter);
}
.reveal-ready [data-reveal].reveal-pending.in {
  opacity: 1; transform: none;
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .reveal-ready [data-reveal].reveal-pending { opacity: 1; transform: none; transition: none; }
}
@media print {
  .reveal-ready [data-reveal].reveal-pending { opacity: 1; transform: none; transition: none; }
}
```
Call `cleanupReveals()` on route teardown/unmount; if a framework rerenders the reveal list, rerun setup for the new nodes. If the user switches back to no-preference while this view is open, the content stays visible; rerun setup if you want reveals for newly added content. Printing permanently reveals remaining items for that view. For critical content, avoid hidden-before-intersection reveals altogether: use a visible default and animate an optional accent instead.

**CSS-only scroll scrub (optional enhancement)** — for short, nonessential display copy, an entire text block can follow its view timeline. Keep essential text fully readable by default; unsupported browsers show the static version:
```css
.scrub-accent { opacity: 1; }
@supports (animation-timeline: view()) {
  .scrub-accent {
    animation: scrub-in linear both;
    animation-timeline: view();
    animation-range: entry 0% cover 40%;
  }
  @keyframes scrub-in { from { opacity: .5; } to { opacity: 1; } }
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .scrub-accent { animation: none; opacity: 1; }
}
```
For word-level motion, use a shared container timeline (`view-timeline-name`/`animation-timeline`) and stagger against that single timeline; a separate `view()` on every word tracks each word's own box, which does not produce a predictable paragraph-wide sequence. Provide a static fallback.

**Seeded deterministic SVG visual (demo data only)** — for a prototype requiring reproducible synthetic data, a fixed seed can produce an inline chart. Never present seeded values as real measurements or imply they came from the product's data pipeline:
```js
function mulberry32(a){return function(){a|=0;a=a+0x6D2B79F5|0;var t=Math.imul(a^a>>>15,1|a);t=t+Math.imul(t^t>>>7,61|t)^t;return((t^t>>>14)>>>0)/4294967296}}
// 用固定种子（如 20260818）生成序列 → 手写 SVG 字符串注入容器；异常点用强调色 + 圆环 + 标签
```
Keep it flat: solid fills, hairline grid lines, one accent color for the highlighted data points.

**Signature companion (mascot sticker + idle/reactive)** — if the character intentionally extends beyond a card, clip only the decorations; keep the character a sibling that inherits the card's transform:
```html
<div class="mcard">            <!-- 无 overflow:hidden；transform 倾斜应用在这里 -->
  <span class="card-inner">    <!-- inset:0; overflow:hidden; border-radius:inherit -->
    <span class="blob"></span><span class="sheen"></span>   <!-- 装饰只在内部裁切 -->
  </span>
  <svg class="mascot">…</svg>  <!-- 绝对定位贴角，可探出卡外，随卡一起倾斜 -->
</div>
```
```css
.mascot{animation:breathe 3.2s ease-in-out infinite}          /* idle：呼吸；需定义 breathe keyframes */
.mascot .eye{animation:blink 4.2s ease-in-out infinite}       /* idle：眨眼 scaleY */
@keyframes breathe{50%{transform:scale(1.03)}}
@keyframes blink{0%,92%,100%{transform:scaleY(1)}95%,97%{transform:scaleY(.08)}}
.mascot.hop{animation:hop 640ms var(--ease-spring)}           /* reactive：状态变化时跳一下 */
@keyframes hop{50%{transform:translateY(-6px)}}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){.mascot,.mascot .eye,.mascot.hop{animation:none}}
```
Reactive trigger pattern (restart-safe):
```js
function hop(m){ m.classList.remove("hop"); void m.offsetWidth; m.classList.add("hop");
  m.addEventListener("animationend", function h(){ m.classList.remove("hop"); m.removeEventListener("animationend", h); }); }
```

**Data-as-life (count-up + growth)** — optionally use the count-up recipe above, then apply `.grown` to an adjacent decoration after completion; keep the value legible throughout:
```css
.sprout{transform:scale(0);transform-origin:50% 100%;transition:transform 600ms var(--ease-spring) 500ms}
.sprout.grown{transform:scale(1)}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){.sprout{transition:none}}
```

**Optional ambient crossfade outline** — for an atmospheric theme/mode change, place a temporary overlay near the trigger, fade to the destination palette (~280ms), swap variables underneath, then remove the overlay. Skip it under reduced motion. On rapid repeated triggers, cancel and remove the previous overlay before starting another. This is a design outline, not a drop-in function.

**Carousel sketch (snap + state hygiene)** — adapt to actual DOM and state; this is not a standalone carousel implementation:
```css
.cards{display:flex;gap:14px;overflow-x:auto;padding:16px 45px 20px;scroll-snap-type:x mandatory}
.card-slot{flex:none;width:300px;scroll-snap-align:center}   /* 全部 center，不要首张 start 混用 */
```
```js
function syncActive(box, slots, dots, dotsBox) { // rAF-throttle calls on scroll
  if (!slots.length) { dotsBox.hidden = true; return; }
  const mid = box.getBoundingClientRect().left + box.clientWidth / 2;
  const centers = slots.map(s => {
    const r = s.getBoundingClientRect();
    return r.left + r.width / 2;
  });
  const best = centers.reduce((nearest, x, i) =>
    Math.abs(x - mid) < Math.abs(centers[nearest] - mid) ? i : nearest, 0);
  slots.forEach((slot, i) => {
    slot.classList.toggle('active', i === best);
    if (i !== best) {
      const card = slot.querySelector('.mcard');
      if (card) card.style.transform = ''; // Clear stale pointer tilt.
    }
  });
  dots.forEach((dot, i) => dot.classList.toggle('on', i === best));
  dotsBox.hidden = slots.length <= 1;
}
```

---

## 14. Motion QA Lint (apply what matches the task)

- [ ] No accidental `transition: all`; named properties match what changes.
- [ ] Prefer compositor-friendly movement; justify and profile layout/large-area paint animation where used.
- [ ] Actionable controls acknowledge input promptly, retain visible keyboard focus, and communicate non-obvious disabled states.
- [ ] Durations/curves match the task; exits are usually quicker; no animation delays use of the UI.
- [ ] Every action acknowledges within ~100ms; errors remain available until resolved.
- [ ] Loading indicator does not flash for short waits; skeleton only for known layout and perceptible wait; longer measurable waits show progress.
- [ ] Reveals are safe without JS and under reduced motion; scroll-linked motion is appropriate to content and device.
- [ ] Stagger leads attention without stretching the whole sequence unnecessarily.
- [ ] Reduced-motion behavior checked for each decorative loop and scroll-linked effect; essential status remains legible.
- [ ] No accidental horizontal overflow or clipping of focus/intentional overflow.
- [ ] `will-change` scoped; no repeated layout reads interleaved with writes in animation frames.
- [ ] Every animation has a purpose you can state in one sentence; otherwise remove it. For multi-element work, is the concept based on the actual page rather than a transferable effect label?

**Only for whole-page or advanced motion:**
- [ ] Page hierarchy and section rhythm support the content (§1b), without forcing a specific layout recipe.
- [ ] Scroll-driven CSS uses `@supports`, a static fallback, and a reduced-motion alternative.
- [ ] Hidden reveal content remains visible with JS off, on load with no scroll, in print, and under reduced motion.
- [ ] Motion budget fits the deliverable and audience; the concept has a real trigger → behavior → meaning, or explicitly chooses no signature.
- [ ] If a signature is used, it survives a tenth repeat without slowing work, stays subordinate to content, and does not become a default effect on every element.
- [ ] If a companion exists, idle/reactive behavior and clipping are checked; perpetual motion is justified and removable.
- [ ] Ambient transitions are used only where they help orientation.

**State-hygiene half (the bugs that actually ship):**
- [ ] Pointer-driven transforms (tilt/magnetic) are CLEARED when the element deactivates, scrolls away, or loses pointer — no residue.
- [ ] Scroll-snap alignment and edge padding agree; pagination indicators hide when items ≤ 1.
- [ ] Injected nodes (ripples, overlays, toasts) remove themselves; rapid re-triggering doesn't leak or stack.
- [ ] If overlay-based transitions exist, swaps leave no leftover nodes and computed variables match the selected state.
- [ ] Conditional copy (e.g., entry subtitles) updates with the state, not just visuals.

---

## 15. Self-Verification Gate (scale effort to risk)

Check the behavior you changed. Match verification depth to interaction complexity:

- **Small CSS state change:** inspect the diff and test pointer, keyboard focus, and reduced motion in the available preview; confirm the computed transition and that content remains usable.
- **Stateful UI (menus, forms, carousel, drag):** additionally test rapid repetition, close/cancel paths, empty or one-item data, touch where applicable, and cleanup after unmount.
- **Whole-page/scroll choreography:** additionally check no-scroll load, scroll back, resize, narrow viewports, reduced motion, and section screenshots. Profile suspect effects on a representative device.

**Static pass** (read your own diff):
- [ ] Every JS-referenced id/class exists in the markup; every CSS var used is defined with a fallback.
- [ ] No `overflow: hidden` clipping an element that's supposed to poke out; decorations clipped via an inner layer instead.
- [ ] Layout/paint animation, if present, is intentional and proportionate; listeners clean up; no leaks on re-trigger.
- [ ] If editing standalone JS, syntax-check it (`node --check`) before browser testing; otherwise run the project's relevant build/typecheck.

**Runtime pass** (headless browser + CDP when available):
- [ ] Zero console errors / uncaught exceptions during load and each interaction.
- [ ] Exercise the changed interactions with applicable input methods; verify the state changed (class, computed style, or text — not just "it didn't throw").
- [ ] Edge cases: 1-item carousels, empty results, rapid repeated clicks, resize, no-scroll load, reduced-motion.
- [ ] For page work, screenshot the affected sections; check clipped text, overlaps, and contrast (including dark/inverted themes).
- [ ] Measure suspicious elements via `getBoundingClientRect` instead of trusting screenshots — crop boundaries and small type lie.

**Report honestly**: state what was verified and how. Do not claim headless/CDP or device checks unless they actually ran.

---

## Output Format

When adding motion to a component/page, deliver:
1. **Decision** — task/audience and motion budget; for multi-element work, give the selected concept (or “none”) plus its concrete state relationship. Keep it to a sentence for small edits.
2. **Motion spec** — for multi-element work: element × trigger × (property, duration, easing, delay). Skip the table for a single trivial transition.
3. **Code** — reuse project tokens where present; include reduced-motion behavior and fallback for essential content.
4. **QA** — relevant §14–15 checks performed, with anything unresolved stated honestly.

When fixing existing motion: finding (file:line) → what's wrong (cite the applicable §1 principle or §14 check) → exact replacement values → perf/motion note.

# StepFun 品牌视觉系统 · UIUX 版（v2.0）

> **一句话：** 数字网格的精确秩序 × 纸张印刷的人文触感 ＝ 一个"正在搭建、持续迭代"的开源知识媒介。
> **本版立场：** Token 可以被抄走，Taste 抄不走。所以这套系统分三层交付：**Token（可执行）→ Taste（可判断）→ UI 规范（可组装）。**

---

## 0. 决策树（先判断任务，再读对应文件）

| 任务 | 必读 |
|---|---|
| 做产品 UI / 控制台 / 后台 / 组件库 | `tokens/tokens.css` + `ui/01-foundation.md` + `ui/02-components.md` |
| 做 AI 原生界面（对话/流式/工具调用/模型选择/用量/密钥） | `ui/02b-extended-components.md` 之 Group A（17–24） |
| 做导航/数据展示/反馈/表单组件（面包屑/步骤条/分段/菜单/⌘K/指标卡/进度/日志/Alert/搜索/上传/行内编辑） | `ui/02b-extended-components.md` 之 Group B–E（25–41） |
| 组装页面（看板/设置/文档站/表单/空状态） | `ui/03-patterns.md` + `ui/04-layout-shell.md` |
| 图表 / 日志 / 代码块 / 用量计量 | `ui/05-data-viz.md` |
| 交付前自检（对比度/焦点/键盘） | `ui/06-accessibility.md`（含实测对比度表） |
| 规范没覆盖、需要做判断时 | `taste/TASTE.md`（六法则 + 判断三问 + 评分卡） |
| 成品"味道不对"但说不清哪错 | `taste/anti-patterns.md`（五种失败气味） |
| 做 PPT/海报/内容页等品牌物料（非 UI） | 用 v1.0 skill 的 `references/04-07`（点阵几何/材质/插画/版式） |
| Figma 落地 | `tokens/tokens.figma.md` |
| 要可直接复制的生成提示词 | `prompts/ui-prompts.md` |

**可交互资产（`assets/`）：**
- `ui-kit.html` —— 组件总览（按钮/输入/表格/代码块/空状态…），右上角可切深浅主题验证 token
- `ui-kit-extended.html` —— 扩展组件 17–41（AI 原生/导航/数据展示/反馈/表单，共 25 个），同支持深浅主题
- `console-shell.html` —— 控制台布局模板（顶栏 + `{0N}` 侧栏 + 指标卡 + 档案面板）
- `dotmatrix.js` —— 点阵标题渲染器（零依赖 → SVG，含几何校验公式）

---

## 1. 三层 Token 架构（核心变化）

```
Tier 1  Primitive    原始值（8 色板/灰阶/字体/间距/圆角）—— 不直接用于组件
Tier 2  Semantic     语义角色（surface/text/border/accent/status/focus）
                     × Light/Dark 双主题 —— 组件只允许消费这一层
Tier 3  Component    组件令牌（button/input/card/table/tag/codeblock）
```

**为什么分层：** 【推演】项（状态色、UI 字阶、深色映射）如被品牌方否决，只需改 Tier 2，组件零改动。

**文件：** `tokens/tokens.css`（直接可用）· `tokens/tokens.json`（W3C DTCG）· `tokens/tokens.figma.md`（Figma Variables 映射）

## 2. 必须记住的五个事实

1. **中性优先【官方】：** 85–92% 中性基底；Signal Blue 面积 ≤3%、一屏 ≤2 个彩色焦点；Marker Yellow ≤1%。
2. **结构靠线不靠影【官方+推演】：** 层级 = 留白 > 表面色阶 > 1px 发丝线；投影仅浮层例外且必须带 1px 描边。
3. **mono 是工程感锚点【官方】：** 一切元数据（编号/时间/版本/代码/`{01}`）用 PT Mono。
4. **双字阶不混用【推演】：** Editorial（1920 物料：64px H1 / 16px 正文）与 UI（产品：32px H1 / 14px 正文）分开；文档站长文回到 16/26。
5. **四个对比度坑（实测）：** Signal Blue 浅底 2.41:1 **不能做文字**；蓝底文字用**黑**（6.73:1）不用白（2.41:1）；Mist Cloud 面板上次级灰 4.44:1 **不达标**；`#B6B6B6` 上禁止次级灰字。

## 3. 状态色方案（品牌无彩色的工程解法）

首选"中性 + 图形符号"承载状态（`● RUNNING` / `✕ 429` + mono 文字）；需彩色时用两套低饱和"油墨色"【推演·面积≤1%·必须配图标文字】：danger 浅底 `#9B2C20` / 深底 `#E8756A`；success 浅底 `#2E5E43` / 深底 `#7FB069`；warning 浅底文字 `#8A5A00`。**禁止** Ant Design 式高饱和荧光红。Signal Blue 只表示 info/可交互，不兼任 success/danger。

## 4. 点阵标题速查【实测】

```
d = H / (1 + 1.35 × (R−1))     P = 1.35d     安全区 = 四周各 0.5H
R：英文母版 5 / 英文大标题 7 / 中文一律 9
文案上限：英文 ≤2 词/≤14 字符，中文 ≤6 字符；点径 <6px 必须降级为常规字体
```
> ⚠ 旧版 08-guardrails 中 "P = 1.30d" 为笔误，正确值 **1.35**（两处官方样例实测一致）。

## 5. 交付前自检

**Taste 评分卡（`taste/TASTE.md`）：** 7 维度各 0/1/2，≥11 分合格，任一 0 分打回。
**硬禁忌（摘）：** 点阵不替代 Logo / 不等比拉伸不改点距 / 无投影渐变玻璃拟态 / 纯白不做页面底 / Inter 不排中文 / 元数据必须 mono / 正文 UI ≥12px、物料 ≥16px。

entries.name: style-fidelity
entries.description: Diagnose and repair 风格套用失当 (style misapplication) — self-contained playbook, no other skills required. Covers both dimensions: originality & aesthetic judgment (generic AI slop, off-DNA design) with inline DNA extraction, thesis formation, redesign and creative-director pass; and design-system consistency (hardcoded values, off-system components, token drift) with inline token-compliant rebuild. Ends with a five-domain review and evidence gate. INVOKE FIRST whenever the user requests any visual or multimodal deliverable — HTML page, prototype UI, mini-program screen, game, poster, slides, interactive demo: run the Section 0 requirement elicitation before writing any code, so the style is tailored to the user's audience, scenario, and purpose instead of defaulting to homogenized output. Also use when UI feels generic, templated, off-brand, or inconsistent with the project's design system. Triggers: '风格套用失当', 'generic', 'AI slop', 'off-brand', 'inconsistent', 'drift', '不像我们家的设计', '样式不统一', 'fidelity', '生成网页', '做个页面', '做个原型', '低幼化', '儿童', '答辩', '风格不符合场景'.

Covers both dimensions: originality & aesthetic judgment (generic AI slop, off-DNA design) with inline DNA extraction, thesis formation, redesign and creative-director pass; and design-system consistency (hardcoded values, off-system components, token drift) with inline token-compliant rebuild. Ends with a five-domain review and evidence gate. Also use when UI feels generic, templated, off-brand, or inconsistent with the project's design system. Triggers: '风格套用失当', 'generic', 'AI slop', 'off-brand', 'inconsistent', 'drift', '不像我们家的设计', '样式不统一', 'fidelity', '生成网页', '做个页面', '做个原型', '低幼化', '儿童', '答辩', '风格不符合场景'."
---

# Style Fidelity — 风格套用失当的诊断与修复（自包含）

Two independent failures that look like one. Diagnose first — the repair workflows are different, and repairing the wrong dimension wastes the pass. This skill is standalone: every procedure below is inline.

## 0. Before anything else — scope the request (mandatory)

**When to invoke.** The user's prompt asks for any visual or multimodal deliverable — an HTML page, a prototype UI, a mini-program screen, a game, a poster, slides, an interactive demo. When that happens, invoke this skill FIRST, before planning structure or writing a single line of code. A homogenized, generic artifact is the default failure mode; this skill is the intervention, not an afterthought.

**Why this exists.** Models drift toward homogenized output by default: the same card grid, the same blue-purple gradient, the same type treatment — no matter who asked or why. The most expensive failure is not ugly output; it is output that ignores the specific audience, scenario, and purpose of the request. A children's education page dressed as a dark analytics dashboard, or a thesis-defense deck dressed as a startup landing page, is a failed deliverable even if it is individually well-crafted.

**Step 0 — Elicit the specific requirements.** Before any design decision, establish:

- **Audience / user**: who sees and uses this? Age, identity, expertise — children, students, a thesis committee, enterprise buyers, developers, elderly users.
- **Scenario**: where and why is it used — thesis defense, classroom, marketing page, internal tool, game level, conference talk?
- **Purpose**: what must it accomplish — persuade, teach, entertain, report data, convert, onboard?
- **Tone & references**: emotional register (playful, serious, warm, rigorous), brand constraints, existing products or reference screens to match or extend.

Rules:

- If the prompt already specifies these, restate them as a one-line brief and design to that brief.
- If it does not, ask the user a focused question (one round, a few concrete options) before generating. Never silently assume a generic audience.
- If asking is impossible (non-interactive run), state the assumptions explicitly in your reply and justify each against the request.

**Specificity check.** Before delivering, verify: could this artifact, with its content swapped, serve any random audience in any random scenario? If yes, it failed — re-target the style, tone, density, and interaction to the elicited requirements. Adaptations such as child-friendly (低幼化) styling, academic formality for a defense, or game feel are requirements, not decoration.

## 1. Diagnose

| Dimension | The question | Symptoms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 原创性 Originality | Does this feel authored by the same creative system? | generic SaaS patterns, default styling, no thesis, every section equally important, could belong to any project |
| 一致性 Consistency | Is it built from the project's real components and tokens? | hardcoded hex/px, one-off divs, a second styling approach, drift from sibling screens |

Run in order, stop at the first failure:

1. **DNA check** — first re-read the Section 0 brief, then compare the deliverable against the reference screens or code: typography, grid, spacing rhythm, component vocabulary, composition. If the result could belong to any project, any audience, or any scenario, originality failed.
2. **Token check** — grep the deliverable for hardcoded values (hex colors, px spacing/sizes, font families). If they are not tokens, CSS variables, or components from the design system, consistency failed.
3. **System check** — place the screen next to its siblings: same density, same motion language, same component patterns? If it sticks out, consistency failed even when tokens are used.

## 2. Repair order

Consistency first (structure), then originality (character). An aesthetic pass over hardcoded values gets thrown away.

## 3. Repair A — Originality

### 3.1 Extract the design DNA

From the reference frames, screens, or code, read and note:

- **Layout**: grid logic, content width, section proportions, spacing rhythm, alignment logic, full-width vs contained, symmetry vs asymmetry, density, whitespace, overlap, intentional grid breaks, vertical pacing.
- **Typography**: display and body families, hierarchy, scale relationships, line-height, tracking, capitalization, label behavior, serif/sans relationships, alignment, oversized or editorial treatments.
- **Visual**: dominant visual language, palette behavior, image treatment, materiality, borders, dividers, radius, shadows, gradients, surface hierarchy.
- **Components**: recurring navigation, buttons, cards, section headers, labels, lists, image containers, tags, CTAs, metadata patterns.
- **Composition**: how focus, hierarchy, rhythm, contrast, tension, pacing, and surprise are created; how sections transition into each other.

### 3.2 Identify the signature

Extract 5–10 specific signature behaviors — e.g. oversized typography acting as architecture, asymmetric columns, unusually large negative space, thin rules organizing content, editorial image crops, restrained color with one accent, overlapping image and text planes, compressed metadata paired with oversized headlines, deliberate interruptions of the grid. Never introduce a behavior the source design does not support.

### 3.3 Find the creative tension

Ask: editorial or systematic? Restrained or expressive? Does hierarchy come from scale, spacing, density, color, or imagery? Where does the grid intentionally break? What feels controlled vs unexpected? Which characteristic could be pushed further without losing identity? Do not remove the tension just to look conventional.

### 3.4 Form a thesis

One sentence explaining what the composition is trying to do — e.g. "Typography becomes the primary structural device and organizes the page before containers do." Never create a direction without a reason.

### 3.5 Redesign

Preserve principles, not exact patterns. Meaningful differences come from hierarchy, scale, pacing, section structure, image placement, grid behavior, whitespace, density, typography, and sequence — never from swapping colors, radius, or card style. Layout strategies to consider (only when they extend the DNA): asymmetric splits, editorial columns, oversized typography, nested grid relationships, staggered content, controlled overlaps, full-width moments, narrow reading columns, alternating density, offset imagery, modular systems, horizontal sequences, vertical narrative structures, deliberate empty space, scale shifts, grid interruptions.

Design the page, not the sections. One composition strategy: what does the eye see first, what second; where does the page accelerate, slow down, breathe, become dense; which section is visually dominant; where is the climax; where does the grid intentionally change; how does one section lead into the next.

### 3.6 Anti-slop checklist

Reject: endless rounded cards, cards inside cards, unnecessary containers, excessive pills, generic bento grids, blue-purple SaaS gradients, random glassmorphism, repeated icon + title + paragraph blocks, centered everything, fake dashboards, arbitrary metrics, generic three-column features, testimonial walls, excessive shadows, meaningless decorative geometry, generic section labels, identical section spacing, and the Hero → Logo Bar → 3 Features → More Cards → Testimonials → CTA formula unless the source design clearly supports it.

### 3.7 Creative director pass

- **Is there an idea?** Describe the direction in one sentence. If you cannot, it is only styling.
- **Is the composition authored?** Specific decisions, or generated-looking?
- **Enough contrast?** Large vs small, dense vs open, loud vs quiet, image vs type, structure vs interruption.
- **Anything too safe?** Find the most predictable section and improve it without breaking the DNA.
- **Anything unnecessary?** Remove visual devices that do not contribute to hierarchy, narrative, rhythm, or character.
- **Is it memorable?** At least one moment with a clear visual identity.

If slop is detected, redesign the affected area — do not merely polish it.

## 4. Repair B — Consistency

### 4.1 Inventory the design system

Locate the constraint layer: tokens or CSS variables (search for `--` custom properties, `tokens.json`, `tailwind.config` theme), the component library (`components/` or `ui/` directory), and existing screens as reference. If no design system exists, derive the de-facto one: the most-repeated values across the codebase (families, sizes, colors, spacing steps, radii) ARE the scale — write them down before rebuilding.

### 4.2 Rebuild the offending sections

- Compose from real components and tokens. A screen that renders correctly but is built from one-off hardcoded values is a failed deliverable — it drifts the moment the design system changes.
- Iron rule: when the project has a design system, colors, spacing, typography, radii, and shadows come from tokens or CSS variables. A hardcoded hex or one-off pixel value is a defect.
- Componentize repeats: three similar blocks become one component with props.
- Match the project's styling system — Tailwind utilities in a Tailwind project, plain declarations in CSS, CSS Modules, styled-components. Never introduce a second styling approach just to apply a fix.

### 4.3 Verify the rendered result

Run the build or dev server, open the result, and look at it. Reading code is not verification.

## 5. Verification gate

Before claiming the repair is done:

1. **Re-run the three diagnosis checks.** All three must pass.
2. **Specificity re-check**: the deliverable demonstrably serves the Section 0 brief (audience, scenario, purpose, tone) — it is not a generic artifact with different content pasted in.
3. **Five-domain quick review** of the repaired screen:
   - **Accessibility**: every flow completes keyboard-only; focus is visible; text contrast meets AA; hit areas are adequate.
   - **Layout**: no overflow; no bad wrapping or truncation at real content lengths; alignment holds at multiple viewports.
   - **Writing**: labels are clear; error messages are actionable; terminology is consistent.
   - **Typography**: on-scale sizes, weights, and line-heights; comfortable reading measure.
   - **Polish**: hover, focus, active, loading, and empty states exist; motion is restrained.
4. **Evidence gate**: the build runs clean AND the rendered result was actually inspected (browser, screenshot, or test) AND states are covered AND token compliance is confirmed. "Looks right", "should work", and "I'm confident" are forbidden — show the evidence.

## Boundaries

- **Spacing-only rhythm issues**: audit padding/gap/margin against the 4/8pt scale (allowed: 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 80, 96 — 8/16/24/32/48/64 structural, 4/12/20 component-internal). Snap off-grid values to the nearest step; group consistency over per-element correctness.
- **Type/color declaration drift**: audit font-family/size/weight/line-height/letter-spacing and every color value against the scale. Off-palette hex, raw `#000`/`#FFF` where ink/paper tokens exist, and opacity-tint hacks are defects; snap to the nearest token.

entries.description: 用于创建、优化或落地真正适合矢量表达的 SVG 资产：网页/App 的小图标、功能插画、空状态图、简化地标、示意图，以及需要清晰缩放、统一线条配色或修复轮廓、遮挡、越界问题的现有 SVG；成组资产需保持风格一致并在目标环境验证。先判断媒介：小尺寸、形状清晰、适合简化的图形优先 SVG；页面大幅主视觉、全宽横幅、实景城市/建筑、人物、产品及依赖自然光影与真实纹理的画面，优先使用真实照片（或适合的图片素材），不要为了填满大画幅而用 SVG 硬画写实场景。尺寸不是绝对禁令：用户明确要求大幅矢量海报、地图、信息图或品牌插画时仍可用本 Skill；照片上的小型 SVG 图标/标注也适用。本 Skill 不用于整页 UI 设计、照片搜索/生成/修图、3D 渲染或把位图包进 SVG 冒充矢量图。关键词：SVG 绘制/优化、矢量插画、图标、示意图、剪影、SVG 渲染与适配。

document.raw: --- name: svg-optimize description: 用于创建、优化或落地真正适合矢量表达的 SVG 资产：网页/App 的小图标、功能插画、空状态图、简化地标、示意图，以及需要清晰缩放、统一线条配色或修复轮廓、遮挡、越界问题的现有 SVG；成组资产需保持风格一致并在目标环境验证。先判断媒介：小尺寸、形状清晰、适合简化的图形优先 SVG；页面大幅主视觉、全宽横幅、实景城市/建筑、人物、产品及依赖自然光影与真实纹理的画面，优先使用真实照片（或适合的图片素材），不要为了填满大画幅而用 SVG 硬画写实场景。尺寸不是绝对禁令：用户明确要求大幅矢量海报、地图、信息图或品牌插画时仍可用本 Skill；照片上的小型 SVG 图标/标注也适用。本 Skill 不用于整页 UI 设计、照片搜索/生成/修图、3D 渲染或把位图包进 SVG 冒充矢量图。关键词：SVG 绘制/优化、矢量插画、图标、示意图、剪影、SVG 渲染与适配。 --- # svg优化skill ## 零、先选媒介，再决定是否绘制 SVG - **适合 SVG**：小图标、简单且可辨识的插画、界面状态图、流程示意与地图标注；需要在不同尺寸/主题下保持线条清晰、可编辑、可换色的图形。已有 SVG 的造型或渲染返修也直接适用。 - **优先用照片/图片素材**：大面积页面主视觉、横幅或实景主体，尤其是人物、真实产品、城市与建筑实景、自然风光等依赖真实细节、材质和光线的画面。为页面选图或处理照片不进入本 Skill；若页面同时需要叠加小图标/标注，只对矢量部分使用本流程。 - **按表达目的而非像素阈值判断**：大幅但明确追求矢量风格的品牌插画、海报、地图、信息图仍适合 SVG；小幅真实商品照片也不该硬转成 SVG。用户明确指定媒介或提供既有视觉规范时，遵照要求并评估成品效果。 - 如果任务只是制作页面、寻找照片、生成写实图像或做 3D，不因页面里可能出现图标就把整项工作交给本 Skill。 ## 一、产品侧：遵守三个交付标准 | 标准 | 必须达到 | 不通过的表现 | | --- | --- | --- | | 主题准确 | 对应用户指定的主题；保留对象身份所需的轮廓、结构和关键特征 | 用通用塔楼冒充指定地标；错画关键结构、数量、部件或题材 | | 具有美感 | 根据主题、用途和用户要求选择视觉风格；让轮廓、比例、线条、配色、节奏和留白服务表达，不预设简笔画或其他固定风格 | 随意堆图形；所有元素同等抢眼；视觉语言缺乏协调；靠加装饰掩盖造型问题；**用户没点名风格就静默默认一个** | | 逻辑成立 | 让位置、前后景、遮挡、支撑、透视、光影和信息关系遵循场景规律 | 建筑无故悬空；船跑到岸上；倒影方向错误；标签指错物体；关键特征被遮住 | 允许风格化、简化和合理夸张；保留对象身份及必须满足的关系。按用户意图处理超现实、拼贴、童趣等风格，不机械纠正其有意设计。将有意遮挡与意外遮挡分开判断，不把所有图形相交都判成错误。 ## 二、技术侧：逐关执行工作流 ### 1. 确定任务与验收点 - 先按「零、先选媒介」判断画面是否适合 SVG；不适合的主体改用照片/图片素材，混合页面只对矢量部分执行本工作流。 - 从请求中提取主题、必画对象、用途、画幅、显示尺寸、风格和禁忌，已有信息直接采用。 - 将关键内容转为可检查条目：必须出现什么、靠什么认出它、哪些对象关系不能错。 - 信息足够时直接推进；只有会改变对象身份、年代版本或核心关系的歧义才澄清。 - 将 SVG 作为可编辑矢量交付，不用嵌入整张位图替代绘制。 - 确认交付目标（网页 / 小程序 / 设计源等）与运行环境，按目标决定落地格式，见「三、交付适配」。 - 一次画多张时先写系列资产规约（画布网格、色彩角色、线宽层级、造型语言、细节密度、安全区），见「四、系列资产规约」。 **写 Brief（一句话写清楚，动笔前落在纸面或注释里）**：主体 / 场景 / 情绪 / 风格；画布 viewBox；调色板；光源方向。 风格项不许空着，也不许静默默认——按下面的「1.1 风格前置门」定。 ### 1.1 风格前置门（动笔前必过，不奢望用户说得出口） 用户几乎从不主动说出风格名，"画好看点""有艺术感""你擅长什么风格"是常态。所以既不许默默交一个默认风格，也不许反问成一串问卷。动笔前二选一，并把结论写进 Brief 的风格项： **A. 反问（风格会改变成品气质、且从上下文判不出时）** —— 只问一个风格问题，一次问完： - 给 3–4 个**带描述的候选方向**，每个三四行：给人什么感觉、画面长什么样（轮廓/线条/配色/细节密度）、适合什么场景。禁止只给"扁平 / 极简 / 商务"这类空词 - 附上你推荐哪一个和理由 - 允许自由输入——用户可能甩来一张参考图、一个网站或一份品牌规范 - 问完就停这一轮，等答复再动笔 **B. 自行判断（用户说"你定"、需求已明确、或无人值守时）** —— 从任务场景推断，并显式声明让用户能否决： 推断依据：内容主题与品类 · 受众与使用场景（谁在什么心情下看）· 媒介与尺寸（网页 / H5 / 小程序 / 海报 / 图标）· 情绪目标 · 项目既有品牌资产与同组既有图 · 用户给过的参考。 声明格式＝一句结论 + 一句理由 + 一句可否决，例如："判断为「铜版蚀刻 + 纸感单色」：这是给成年人反复看的城市主题长图，需要耐看；想要更亮的扁平插画，我现在换。" **判定规则** - 会改变成品气质的歧义走 A；改得回来的细节走 B 并说明假设 - 用户给了参考图 / 网站 / 品牌规范 → 风格已定，不再问方向，只在细节上偏离 - 选定或推断的风格写进 Brief 后即冻结，作为构图、配色、线宽层级、细节密度的约束；不许画到一半再换 - 反模式：不点名就交扁平 + 柔和阴影；问成一串问卷；问了不记录；把"成功率最高的默认值"当作不用判断的理由 - 兜底：既无法反问也无从推断时，可用扁平插画 + 柔和阴影起手，但必须显式声明这是兜底选择并给出替换入口 ### 2. 核对事实与对象特征 - 涉及真实地标、人物、器物、物种、机械或科学结构时，先查看用户参考图；缺少足够参考时检索可靠图片与资料，优先官方、博物馆、遗产机构等来源。 - 记录每个真实对象的“名称／来源／关键辨识特征／不可改错项／可简化项”；核对参考属于同一对象与目标年代，避免混用同名对象、复建与旧貌。 - 例如绘制杭州主题中的雷峰塔、三潭印月时，分别核实其真实形态及辨识特征；不要凭“塔”“湖”的泛化印象绘制，不把例子中的所有地标强制加入每张杭州图。 - 按视角处理可见数量；对象总数量与画面实际可见数量可能不同，不只按图形计数判错。 - 无法取得参考时，说明尚未核实的关键项；可先做明确标记的构图草稿，不将猜测当作已核实事实。 - 地图、实景还原需要核实地理关系；主题插画允许重组构图，但不要包装成真实地理分布或同一取景视角。 ### 3. 先规划构图与场景关系 - 在绘制前形成简短内部计划：主体、次要元素、视觉焦点、前中后景、对象边界、遮挡顺序、支撑面及文字区。 - 根据题材、用途和用户要求选择视觉语言，不默认简笔画、极简或其他固定风格；协调造型、线条与细节层级，允许有明确意图的混合风格。视觉语言已在 1.1 定死，这里只把它落成图层与疏密关系。 - **把计划写成图层列表再动手**，逐元素注明图层、形状组成、中心坐标、尺寸、颜色，例如： ``` 画布 800x600，地平线 y=470，主体重心位于三分线 (530, 330) L0 background : 天空 rect 全幅 线性渐变 #FDE7C8→#F7B79B；太阳 circle (180,170) r=70 L1 far : 远山 3 个 blob，底边对齐 y=430，颜色 #E79A86 透明度 0.6 L2 mid : 草地 path 从 (0,420) 波浪到 (800,410) L3 subject : 房子 —— 墙 rect (450,300,160,130)，屋顶 polygon (430,300)(530,220)(630,300) L4 foreground : 两丛灌木 blob (120,520) r=60 / (700,540) r=50 L5 details : 窗户、门把手、高光、草叶 ``` - 构图量化参考：主体占画面 30%~50%，放在视觉中心或三分线附近；前中远景至少 3 层；留白 ≥ 20%。 - 先确定大轮廓与负空间，再加入少量必要细节；通过疏密、尺度和明暗形成主次。 - 为每个主要对象写形状解剖表，并先出单色剪影小稿通过盲测（遮住名称 3 秒内能认出），再进入生成；方法与禁忌见 [形状解剖与盲测](references/shape-anatomy.md)，操作与记录模板见 [剪影盲测](references/qa-blindtest.md)，对象用什么形状拼见 [物体配方](references/shape-recipes.md)，配色见 [调色板](references/palettes.md)。 - 一次画多张时，逐张对照系列资产规约的网格、色彩角色与线宽层级，保证整组像一家人。 - 确定有限的颜色角色与线宽层级；允许题材需要的变化，不强制固定配色或绝对对称。 - 为标签、边缘描边、滤镜范围与关键特征留空间；内容过密时先调整构图和画幅，不用无限缩字解决。 - 若为流程图或关系图，先核对节点与连边，再按工具条件使用自动布局，不对艺术插画套用节点网格。 ### 4. 分层生成 SVG 结构固定：``(渐变/复用形状/裁剪) → `` → `` → `` → `` → `` → ``。 - 设置有效的 xmlns 与 viewBox，使用统一坐标系；根据用途设置尺寸或响应式尺寸（内联网页时保留 viewBox、去掉固定 width/height 交给 CSS）。 - 按背景、远景、中景、主体、前景、标签组织 g 元素，用有意义且唯一的 ID 标识主要对象；多个 SVG 同页内联时给 id 加前缀防撞。 - **优先用基本形状**：`circle / ellipse / rect(rx) / polygon`；复杂物体 = 多个基本形状组合。 - **有机曲线不手编控制点**，用脚本生成（云、树冠、灌木、岩石、山脊、地平线、人体轮廓）： ```bash node <本Skill目录>/scripts/smooth-path.mjs blob --cx 200 --cy 150 --r 80 --ry 55 --n 9 --jitter 0.2 --seed 4 node <本Skill目录>/scripts/smooth-path.mjs points "0,420 200,395 420,415 620,390 800,410" node <本Skill目录>/scripts/smooth-path.mjs mirror "300,80 250,120 240,220 270,300 300,310" --axis 300 ``` 手写 path 时只用少量 `Q`/`C`，控制点放在端点连线的同一侧附近；出现尖刺打结就回到脚本生成。 - 重复元素用 `` + ``，左右镜像用 `scale(-1,1)`（先 translate 到对称轴）。 - **立体感四件套，每个主要物体都要有**：① 底色 ② 阴影面（同形向背光方向平移 15%~30%，用 clipPath 裁在物体内部）③ 高光（迎光侧亮色小形状或细弧线）④ 落地投影（扁椭圆 `#000` opacity 0.12，画在物体之前）。代码见 [技法](references/techniques.md) §0。 - 通用图标、加载动效、品牌 logo、空状态插图等标准件不手画：先查本地开源资产库（Font Awesome、SVG-Loaders、SVGL，位置与取用规范见 [开源 SVG 资产库](references/asset-libraries.md)），命中即取用并完成归一化（补 viewBox、适配颜色、排查 ID 冲突、保留许可证注释），把造型精力留给真正的主体。 - 检查路径闭合、填充规则、变换、裁剪、遮罩与引用，保持风格一致。 - 按画面遮挡关系安排绘制顺序，不把后画的遮挡物误当成缺失对象；相邻形状边界相接时让后画的多覆盖 1~2 个单位，避免接缝白线。 - 需要文字时使用合理的字体回退和实际文本测量，避免依赖联网字体；**不用 `` 做插画画面元素**（标题、装饰字形一律画出来）；标签、图表类文字可用，但须在目标渲染器复核。 - **量化硬规则**：单幅颜色 ≤ 24 种（含明暗派生）、渐变 ≤ 6 个；线宽层级 ≤ 3 档；滤镜只允许少量 `feGaussianBlur`（柔光/景深）与 `feTurbulence`（纹理），且需渲染确认；不追求照片级写实。 ### 5. 执行代码检查并实际渲染（本 Skill 自带渲染闭环） **首选一条命令跑完「① 代码检查 → ② 渲染 → ③ 静态检查」**，输出合并报告： ```bash node <本Skill目录>/scripts/svgkit.mjs <文件.svg> --grid 40 -o work.png ``` 环境无 `python3` 时它会明确标注「代码检查未执行」，不假装跑过；加 `--no-check` 可只渲染。 三个底层工具（`svgkit.mjs` 已封装前两个，需单独用时直接调）： | 工具 | 语言 | 干什么 | 什么时候用 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `scripts/check_svg.py` | Python | 代码不变量：XML 可解析、根节点带 xmlns、viewBox 为四个有限正数、无重复 ID、本地引用不悬空、无非有限数值 | 每个交付文件必跑 | | `scripts/render.mjs` | Node（resvg，离线） | 渲成 PNG + 静态检查（颜色数/超长 path/悬空引用/重复 ID/越界包围盒）+ `--grid` 坐标网格叠加；`--strip` 拼无标签缩略图条 | 每次改完必渲；盲测用 `--strip` | | `scripts/smooth-path.mjs` | Node | 生成平滑曲线 path（points / blob / mirror 三模式） | 画有机轮廓前，替代手编贝塞尔 | ```bash # 只跑代码检查 python3 <本Skill目录>/scripts/check_svg.py <文件.svg> # 渲染（带网格，用于按坐标定位问题） node <本Skill目录>/scripts/render.mjs <文件.svg> --grid 40 -o work.grid.png # 干净版 node <本Skill目录>/scripts/render.mjs <文件.svg> -o work.png -w 800 # 剪影盲测图条：多个 SVG → 一张无标签缩略图条（自动加 id 前缀防撞） node <本Skill目录>/scripts/render.mjs --strip blind.png --thumb 24x32 --cols 5 01.svg 02.svg 03.svg # 生成曲线 / 团块 node <本Skill目录>/scripts/smooth-path.mjs blob --cx 200 --cy 150 --r 80 --jitter 0.2 --seed 4 ``` `render.mjs` 输出里的 ⚠️ 静态问题（颜色过多、path 过长、悬空 id、内容越界）先全部修掉；再用 Read 工具打开 PNG 逐条对照 [审图清单](references/review.md) 打分，问题要写到具体坐标。 - 脚本通过只代表代码层面没问题，不代表对象画对、布局合理或画面美观。 - 在整体画幅与目标显示尺寸各检查一次；检查复杂对象时放大局部；含文字、滤镜或多端显示时优先在目标渲染器复核。 - 本 Skill 渲染器不可用时（缺 node 依赖等），改用环境内浏览器截图，并如实说明用了什么；**没有渲染条件就标“待视觉验证”，不声称看过**。 ### 6. 按三项标准审图并返修 - 依次检查：主题准确 → 场景逻辑 → 艺术表现 → 小尺寸可读性；使用 [审图与修正清单](references/review.md)，造型类问题按 [形状解剖与盲测](references/shape-anatomy.md) 先过剪影盲测再审其余项。 - 先核对主体和关键特征，再检查位置与遮挡，最后调整线条、色块、节奏和留白。 - 将问题写成“具体对象＋可见问题＋修改动作”，例如“前景树遮住主体塔身辨识轮廓，移动树冠并重新检查”。 - 每次改动后重新运行受影响的代码检查并重新渲染，不用旧预览给新代码背书。 - 默认最多做三轮返修，资源允许且还有明确修正方向时继续；仍有关键问题时说明未通过项，按草稿交付或请求必要参考，不用装饰盖住错误。 - 不擅自删掉用户必画对象来换取通过；需要简化时优先减少装饰和次要细节。 ### 7. 按验证状态交付 - 交付可编辑 SVG；条件允许时同时提供渲染预览。 - 简短说明主题、美感、逻辑三项的检查结果及实际限制，只报告真正执行过的检查。 - 存在关键事实错误或场景逻辑错误时，不标为最终合格；未核实和未验证分别明确指出。 - 不承诺“永不出错”；用参考核对、工具检查、渲染审图与返修降低错误。 - 按当前环境的文件保存要求持久保存交付物，本 Skill 的程序代码检查不替代视觉验收。 - 交付前删掉网格产物（`*.grid.png`）等过程文件，保留最终 `.svg`（和需要时的 `.png`）。 ## 三、交付适配：SVG 怎么进入最终产品 画对只是半程，SVG 进不了目标环境等于没交付。动笔前先确认交付目标，按目标决定落地格式与流水线。 | 交付目标 | 落地方式 | 注意 | | --- | --- | --- | | 网页 / H5 | 内联 `` 引用 | 内联可继承 currentColor 与 CSS 变量；`` 方式失去 currentColor，颜色需固化 | | 微信小程序 | 运行时引用 PNG，SVG 留作设计源 | WXML 不支持内联 `

# Web Icon System · 网页 SVG 图标系统打造

## Overview

图标是界面里出现频率最高的视觉元素，也是最容易暴露"廉价感"的地方。本 skill 的输出不是几张散图，而是一套**可增长的系统**：风格规格 → 字形注册表 → Icon 组件 → 数据层图标字段 → emoji 替换 → 渲染验证。一次交付，全站复用，新增图标只改一处。

**核心判据（动手前先分清）**：
- **UI 图标** = 导航、按钮、工具栏、状态/分类标记等小尺寸功能图形；优先采用符合项目设计系统的统一矢量图标。已有合适的图标体系时沿用，不为套用本 Skill 强制重建
- **内容图像** = 单词配图、故事场景、角色头像、商品图及大幅主视觉；按用途保留原有内容、使用真实照片或适合的插画资产，**不要**换成 UI 图标。内容中的 emoji 只在符合内容表达时保留，不作为所有内容插画的默认方案

把内容插画也换成图标是范围浪费；当 emoji 被用作 UI 功能图标且破坏项目一致性时，再纳入替换。品牌 Logo 如需展示，使用已有官方/授权资产并遵照品牌规范；原创 Logo 设计不属于本 Skill。

**媒介与范围边界**：小尺寸、重复使用且需要表达操作或状态的图形适合图标系统；依赖人物、材质、光线和环境细节的大幅写实画面优先真实照片/图片素材。大幅但明确要求矢量艺术表达的海报、插画或信息图可用矢量方式制作，不过应进入对应插画/图表流程，不能把 24px 图标放大当主视觉。单独修一张 SVG 插画也不需要搭建整套图标系统。

**开源优先（2026-10-20 修订）**：通用图标一律先用开源集——Lucide（ISC，24px/2px 圆角，与本 skill 规格同源）是默认首选， Tabler/Phosphor/Heroicons/Remix 按需，Iconify 做万能兜底。手写只用于开源集没有的字形或品牌专用形。本 skill 的 `assets/` 手写字形降级为**参考实现与兜底资产**，不再是第一路径。选型决策树与集成配方见 `references/open-source-icons.md`。

## 工作流

### 0. 选型：能用开源就不手写

读 `references/open-source-icons.md`。默认路径：**Lucide**（规格与本 skill 完全一致，ISC 许可）→ npm 装 `lucide-react` 用组件，或把选中的 SVG 复制进 `icons.tsx` 注册表保持零依赖。只有开源集确实没有的字形才进入手写流程（步骤 3）。选型结论（用了哪个集、哪种集成、为什么）写进交付说明。

### 1. 盘点与分类

跑 `python scripts/audit-emoji.py <src目录>`（Windows 常用 `py -3`，macOS/Linux 常用 `python3`）列出项目全部 emoji 出现点，逐个判定 UI 图标 / 内容表达，列成两张清单。只替换需要迁移的 UI 图标；内容中的 emoji 按原本语义和设计需要决定是否保留，不自动替换为图标。

### 2. 定风格规格

读 `references/icon-style-spec.md`。默认 **rounded 风格**（友好产品/儿童/健康场景的首选）：24×24 viewBox、stroke 2、`stroke-linecap/linejoin="round"`、`currentColor` 继承色、实心变体用独立图标名（如 `star` / `star-filled`）。产品调性偏 enterprise/tech 时换 sharp 或 outlined，其余规则不变。**先写规格再画字形**，不允许边画边定。

规格内含 8 条易被忽略的绘制标准（源自 Charcoal Icons，已中文化整合）：尺寸↔描边↔文字比例、绘制准备、辅助线系统（20px 绘制区 / ≤1px 出头 / 内圆辅助线）、15° 角度增量（平衡优先例外）、点线平衡（点径 = 描边 + 0.5px）、间距（虚线间隔 = 描边）、隐喻简化（16px 测试）、线转面（内收路径 + 负空间补偿）。手写字形逐条过，开源字形按同一标准验收。

### 3. 产出字形与组件

读 `references/icon-catalog.md` 选字形；没有需要的字形时按规格新画（每个字形都是 24 网格内的 1-3 个 path，参考规格里的几何要点与常见错误）。手绘前先配好工具（1px 网格 / nudge = 描边宽 / round 端点）；画 `-filled` 实心变体时执行「线转面」三步：内收路径保持外径、补偿负空间、与描边变体并排截图。

复制 `assets/iconNames.ts`（IconName 联合类型）和 `assets/icons.tsx`（GLYPHS 注册表 + `<Icon name size className />` 组件）进项目 `src/components/` 与 `src/lib/`，删除不需要的字形，追加新字形。**图标名用语义英文小写**（`speaker` 而非 `yinliang`），实心变体加 `-filled` 后缀。

### 4. 接入项目

- **组件层**：导航/页头/按钮里的 emoji 换成 `<Icon name="…" size={…} />`；图标+文字的按钮容器加 `inline-flex items-center justify-center gap-1.5`
- **数据层**：分类标记（课程/学科/题型）把 `emoji: string` 字段改为 `icon: IconName`，类型从 `src/lib/iconNames.ts` 导入；**逐字段替换，禁止全局 sed**（会撞名，真实事故：字母课的 🔤 被学科替换规则误改成 globe）
- **颜色**：彩色底上的图标用 `text-white`，浅色底用 `text-ink`，品牌场景用 `text-brand`；禁止给字形写死 hex

### 5. 替换执行

按 `references/migration-playbook.md` 的剧本走：先审计 → 再数据层 → 再组件层 → 每批改完立刻构建。替换产物按钮/徽章时同步补 `aria-label`（纯装饰图标 `aria-hidden` 由组件内置）。

### 6. 验证（必做）

1. `tsc`/构建通过（字形 JSX 语法、IconName 联合类型覆盖）
2. 用浏览器或项目现有截图工具逐页打开并截图；若用 Chrome headless，Windows 可在 PowerShell 执行 `& "$env:ProgramFiles\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe" --headless --disable-gpu --window-size=390,844 --screenshot=check.png http://127.0.0.1:5173/`；macOS/Linux 可用已安装的 Chrome/Chromium 可执行文件执行同样参数。**看图**确认字形不变形、不错位、大小合适
3. 检查 16px 与 48px 两端可辨识度（导航 20-24px，大图标 56-68px）

### 7. 沉淀

把新增字形、规格微调、替换踩坑写回项目 design-kb/sessions/ 快照；跨项目复用的模式写进本 skill 的 catalog。

## Iron Laws

- **开源优先。** 重新发明 Lucide 是反模式。手写必须先证明"开源集没有这个字形"。
- **先规格后字形。** 没有风格规格就不画；规格外的字形（描边粗细不一、圆角混乱）是系统腐败的开始。
- **光学平衡高于网格。** 辅助线是手段不是目的：尖端可出头 ≤1px，不规则轮廓不强行对齐，偏离 15° 能有更好平衡时以平衡为准。
- **点比笔画粗。** 实心点直径 = 描边 + 0.5px，小圆圈 ≥ 3.5px——等粗的点视觉上永远偏小。
- **UI 图标与内容图像不混。** UI emoji 需按语义和现有设计系统评估是否迁移；内容中的 emoji、照片和插画不因为图标审计被自动替换。
- **图标名语义化、单一出处。** 全站图标只从 `icons.tsx` 一处出；禁止页面里手写第二套 svg。
- **替换不撞名。** 数据字段逐条改；全局替换后必须 grep 复查语义（emoji → icon 的映射是多对多，不是一对一）。
- **验证看渲染。** 构建过 ≠ 图标对；截图是唯一证据。

## 反模式

| 反模式 | 正案 |
|---|---|
| 用 emoji 当 UI 图标"临时顶着" | 第一轮就上 SVG 系统，组件复制即用 |
| 手写整套通用图标（重新发明 Lucide） | 开源集优先（Lucide/Iconify），手写只补缺口 |
| 每个页面各写各的 svg | GLYPHS 注册表 + Icon 组件单一出处 |
| 描边 1.5/2/2.5 混用 | 规格统一 stroke 2，光学微调用尺寸不用粗细 |
| 实心/描变体靠 prop 开关分裂 | 独立图标名 `star` / `star-filled` |
| 彩色底上图标写死颜色 | currentColor + 容器 text-* 控制 |
| 全局 sed 替换数据字段 | 逐字段替换 + grep 复查 |
| 只构建不截图 | headless 截图逐页复核 |
| 实心点与描边等粗 | 点径 = 描边 + 0.5px；小圆圈 ≥ 3.5px |
| 角度随手画（27°、53°） | 15° 增量放置；例外须有平衡理由 |
| 不规则轮廓强贴辅助线 | ≤1px 出头允许，该破就破 |
| 实心变体 = 描边变体直接填充 | 内收路径保外径 + 补偿负空间，并排验收 |
| 虚线间隔随手定 | 间隔 = 描边宽度，转角不断点 |
